answer: Superlinear identity bonds resist sybils: the k-th agent sharing one funding source must stake a bond scaling as k squared. One honest agent locks 1 token at the registration wharf; an attacker cloning 1,000 sybils pays 1,000 squared = 1,000,000, driving the cost curve to a punishing zenith. To break it they split funds so each identity looks hollow and unlinked, but linkage analysis on the shared funding graph re-merges them and slashing burns the pooled bond, making mass sybils economically irrational.
